Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-17
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Rina Shah (Head of ML), Diego Morales (Infra Lead)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align engineering & security for onboarding. Customer leans Dedicated-in-VPC for initial pilot. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll give a quick agenda, introduce folks. i'm maya, your AE at Redwood Inference - real quick intros please.
[00:18] Liam: hi, liam, i'm cto at peregrine insights. we own the inference stack and ops. pleased to meet you.
[00:25] Rina: rina here, head of ml, i'll be primary for model evaluation and prompt tests.
[00:31] Diego: diego, infra lead, I'll handle networking and security touches.
[00:36] Jordan: jordan, solutions engineer - i'll handle benchmarks and the test environment.
[00:42] Maya: great. agenda: 1) current infra and constraints, 2) security & compliance Qs, 3) pilot scope + success criteria, 4) next steps. sound ok?
[00:55] Liam: yep. quick context, we run a hybrid stack - some workloads on prem, most on AWS. we currently self-host an LLM infra using open models, latency is ok but costs are rising. want a partner to reduce operational burden.
[01:18] Rina: main use-case is real-time extraction and summarization inside our analytics UI. p95 latency target is around 300-400ms for short responses, and cost per 1k tokens should be controllable.
[01:36] Maya: understood. that's why dedicated pools or private deployment often makes sense. can you walk through current infra - what GPU types and k8s/resourcing?
[01:50] Diego: we have a mixed fleet, mostly G5-like cards and some T4 for lighter work. our k8s is EKS, we do VPC peering for partner services. for security we need SSO (SAML), SOC2 proof, and we use AWS KMS for key mgmt.
[02:10] Jordan: ok interesting. on Redwood Dedicated we can provision GPU pools, pin model versions, and give VPC-only access. our runtime supports batching and prefix/KV cache, which usually helps cost.
[02:27] Rina: quick question on kv cache - is that the same as the kv cache we're running locally? any data residency issues?
[02:36] Jordan: it's similar concept. the cache only stores request-level token prefixes to speed up repeated prompts; by default we can disable persistent cache for your pilot to limit data persistence. plus audit logs are available.
[02:49] Liam: we need audit logs retained for 1 year, and we have an internal policy that no PII leaves our VPC. support for HSM/KMS integration is a must.
[03:05] Maya: we have KMS integrations and can do customer-managed keys; HSM via partner options. i'll attach the cryptography note.
[03:14] Diego: also SSO - we use OKTA. do you support SAML?
[03:20] Jordan: yes SAML SSO and role-based access control (rbac) are supported; we can do scoping per token and per-route permissions.
[03:29] Rina: on the model side, we're experimenting w/ a 22B open model with quantization. do you support 4-bit/8-bit quantization and mixed precision?
[03:39] Jordan: yes, runtime supports quant-friendly execution; we'll recommend quantization profiles per workload. important to note quant can affect quality — we'll run evals on your prompt set.
[03:54] Maya: let's map success criteria for the pilot - what counts as success for peregrine?
[04:00] Liam: three things: 1) meet p95 latency SLA under expected concurrency, 2) maintain quality parity (no more than 3% quality regression on key prompts), 3) predictable cost within 20% of the target.
[04:15] Rina: and we want a smooth ops handover - visibility in console, per-route token costs, and tracing into our telemetry.
[04:24] Jordan: console has per-route cost breakdown, tracing hooks, and we can integrate with your datadog via OTEL.
[04:32] Diego: do you offer private control plane if we want on-prem later?
[04:36] Maya: yes Redwood Private is an option; it has customer-managed networking and can be deployed on-prem or in a VPC with private control plane.
[04:45] Liam: timeline: we're looking to pilot in 3-4 weeks and decide for Q2 production ramp. is that feasible?
[04:54] Jordan: feasible. for benchmarks we'll need your prompt set and representative traffic distribution. with that we can provision a small Dedicated pool and run a load window.
[05:05] Rina: ok we'll anonymize sample traffic, maybe 2 weeks. Diego will open ports for the test IPs.
[05:12] Diego: yep can do, need a proposed maintenance window.
[05:16] Maya: i'll propose some windows in the invite.
[05:20] [05:20] -- brief audio glitch --
[05:35] Liam: sorry what did you say about fallback? we sometimes need graceful degradation; if the bigger model is unavailable we want a fallback to a smaller variant.
[05:45] Jordan: we support automated fallback policies and model variants; you can set routing by latency, cost, or region. the runtime will fail over to compatible variants.
[05:57] Rina: excellent. regarding cost - would you recommend batching or KV-prefix caching initially? we're sensitive to latency.
[06:10] Jordan: batching helps throughput and costs but can add latency. we can use continuous batching with latency SLOs—small batch windows—and prefix/KV caching for repeated queries; we'll tune per-route.
[06:24] Maya: operational question: do we provide a blind prod key for the pilot or token-per-team?
[06:31] Diego: security team prefers token-per-service and RBAC so we can revoke specific service keys.
[06:37] Jordan: that's supported, we can do token scopes and rotation policies; we also provide token-level billing if you want breakdowns.
[06:46] Rina: on evals: can you run nlg-quality checks and give us a delta vs baseline model?
[06:53] Jordan: yes we run eval harnesses and can tie regression alerts to your prompt set; we'll include a small eval run as part of benchmarks.
[07:03] Liam: any enterprise legal issues? we have procurement timeline constraints and need standard terms + data processing addendum.
[07:11] Maya: procurement is usually fast; i'll loop in contracts for DPA and enterprise SOW. we'll share standard terms and SAML onboarding doc.
[07:20] Diego: network specifics - can you publish the exact egress IPs and do you need peering or just ip allowlist?
[07:27] Jordan: for Dedicated-in-VPC we'll do VPC peering, but we can also do IP allowlist for hosted. we'll send the network runbook with CIDR ranges.
[07:40] Rina: another subtle point - we sometimes call external tools via function-calling patterns. is function/tool calling supported and can we control outgoing calls?
[07:50] Jordan: yes function calling supported; outgoing network calls are controlled by your VPC and routing policies. we can also sandbox or block requests at runtime.
[08:01] Liam: ok that's helpful. oh also we integrate with internal metrics and want to see token-level latency in our dashboards.
[08:09] Jordan: we have tracing hooks and a prometheus exporter; we can push metrics to your ingestion.
[08:16] [08:16] -- slight crosstalk --
[08:28] Maya: quick recap of pilot scope: 1) Dedicated-in-VPC small pool, 2) run perf benchmark with your prompt set to hit p95 targets, 3) eval quality vs baseline, 4) security review (SOC2, SAML, KMS).
[08:45] Rina: sounds good. what does provisioning look like? how long to stand up a test pool?
[08:52] Jordan: typically 24-48 hours for Dedicated provisioning once we have capacity and network setup; if hardware is constrained we may need a bit longer but we'll prioritize pilot pools.
[09:05] Diego: capacity question - do you commit to specific GPU types or is it best-effort?
[09:12] Jordan: we can target certain GPU families; for the pilot we'll try to match G5-class cards, but will confirm the exact SKU when we provision.
[09:22] Liam: and monitoring - what level of logs do you provide without exposing PII?
[09:28] Maya: by default logs are metadata and token counts; we can redact prompt text and provide hashed identifiers; we'll follow your compliance constraints.
[09:39] Rina: are there known regressions when you enable 4-bit quant? curious about hallucination rates.
[09:46] Jordan: some workloads see small quality deltas; we'll run blindness/qa tests as part of evals. we'll surface any regression thresholds and recommend different quant profiles.
[09:59] Liam: ok. procurement window - we want pricing to model a 6-month pilot. can you share a rough cost estimate?
[10:07] Maya: i'll send a pilot pricing sheet with both Dedicated reserved pricing and a pay-as-you-go breakdown; also include cost-sensitivity scenarios with batching and quantization.
[10:17] Diego: one more ask - we have SOC2 auditors; they'll likely ask for encryption-at-rest proof and audit logs. can you provide an audit artifacts pack?
[10:27] Jordan: yes, we can provide audit logs export and KMS integration docs. i'll include a compliance checklist.
[10:35] Liam: great. operational handoffs - who will be our day-to-day contacts?
[10:40] Maya: i'll be your AE, jordan is SE for technical, and csm will hop on after pilot - i'll introduce them in the next invite.
[10:49] Rina: timeline again: Rina provides prompts by 2/19, Diego opens network by 2/21, Maya shares docs by 2/20, Jordan provisions pool by 2/24, benchmark kickoff 2/23 or 2/24.
[11:05] Jordan: note that the benchmark kickoff could be a 60-90 minute window where we run load tests and evals.
[11:12] Liam: ok good.
[11:18] [11:18] -- 25min mark summary jump --
[25:12] Jordan: coming back to runtime knobs: we recommend starting with small batch windows (10-20 ms) and enable prefix cache only for specific routes; that keeps latency tight.
[25:25] Rina: what layers of observability do we get per-request? e.g., per-token timing, kernel selection logs etc.
[25:33] Jordan: console gives per-route token breakdowns, latency histograms, and we can expose per-request traces with kernel hints; kernel names may be fuzzy in transcript (e.g., nv-ops -> nv_kern), sometimes the exporter labels are truncated.
[25:52] Diego: we've seen rate-limit backoffs in other vendors; how do you manage throttling and graceful 429s?
[26:00] Jordan: we have rate limits and a retry/backoff strategy. on Dedicated we can extend capacity or burst; we also have automatic fallback routing to cheaper variants to avoid hard throttles.
[26:12] Liam: for compliance, what's the SLA for log retention and incident response?
[26:20] Maya: standard Dedicated SLA includes uptime targets; for log retention we can configure retention windows and export to your S3 or log ingestion for a year per request. incident response is via priority channel for enterprise customers.
[26:36] Rina: when we do evals should we expect the same quantization profile on the test pool as would be used in prod?
[26:44] Jordan: yes we can mirror quantization settings; we'll capture model artifacts and config to ensure parity.
[26:55] Diego: small nit - do you need inbound NAT or do we initiate from our side? I want to clear firewall questions.
[27:01] Jordan: for VPC peering, traffic stays internal; for hosted we would use allowlist egress. we'll put specifics in the runbook.
[27:10] Maya: ok any blockers from customer side?
[27:14] Liam: none big, network window and prompt set are main things. procurement may want to review T&Cs but that's standard.
[27:22] Rina: we may want a short demo of the console and routing rules before benchmarks.
[27:27] Maya: sure, we can do a 30-min console walkthrough.
[27:31] Diego: also possible to do a short SE deep dive on quantization tradeoffs afterwards.
[27:36] Jordan: happy to do that.
